answer: Each identity registers one river trap, locks a 70-credit bond to its trap key, and logs weight. Auditors dredge each trap, recover its marble marker, weigh the sediment, and match its serial against the registry; a missing or reused marker, or a shortfall over 5 percent, burns the bond. The first filing costs 31 credits, the kth 31 plus 6 times k minus 1, so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fakes cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-trap ring fails because one dune trap backs one identity and a rented serial is already registered. Honest operators pay 31 once and recover the bond.
